name: MLB-M0 parent baseline
summary: Baseline MLB parent cartridge shell. MLB-M0 owns the daily workflow surface, publish-lane adapters, run manifest, and closeout health gate while the existing side, first-five, first-inning, prop, HR, market-context, and MLB-RP36 relief inputs are migrated behind stable artifacts.
keyImprovements: Names the current MLB parent model as MLB-M0 so future changes can be compared against a stable baseline.
Keeps MLB-RP36 as a relief addendum consumed by MLB-M0 instead of treating the reliever shadow artifact as a separate parent model.
Separates model ownership from workflow plumbing before moving scripts out of the flat pipeline folder.
Adds a May 30 closeout gate so side predictions must flow into `mlb_side_predictions` and `mlb_side_backtests` before postmortem lessons are trusted.
Adds a cartridge-local performance index and quiet-start full-game gate so May 30 failures can affect the next slate instead of staying as notes.
Persists daily hitter platoon split snapshots so the prop model can be audited against the exact split context shown pregame.

keyMetrics.label: Migration status
keyMetrics.details: Prediction behavior is still mostly delegated to pipeline internals, but MLB-M0 owns the public workflow entrypoints, publish-lane adapters, run lock, and model dashboard identity.

keyMetrics.label: Publish adapters
keyMetrics.details: MLB-M0 routes day files, batting impact, lineups, HR, props, sides, veto, training corpus, and history journal exports through cartridge-owned adapters.

keyMetrics.label: Relief addendum
keyMetrics.details: The prior reliever-shadow experiment is tracked as a component consumed by MLB-M0.

keyMetrics.label: May 30 snapshot target
keyMetrics.details: Golden target covers 15 side picks, 49 prop picks, 12 HR picks, 30 reliever-shadow teams, and 15 lineup boards.

keyMetrics.label: May 30 run lock
keyMetrics.details: MLB-M0 now has a file-based run manifest, source lock, input lock, output lock, and snapshot verification target.

keyMetrics.label: May 30 side closeout
keyMetrics.details: Side predictions and backtests are now present in the warehouse for the May 30 golden day.

keyMetrics.label: May 30 result lanes
keyMetrics.details: May 30 exposed a dead-early, low-conversion side failure while first-five and first-inning timing held up better.

keyMetrics.label: Performance index
keyMetrics.details: MLB-M0 now links May 30 run, result, side-board, postmortem, and follow-up artifacts from the cartridge.

notes: MLB-M0 should eventually own the final MLB side, first-five, total, prop, and market-context outputs.
Current implementation internals remain in pipeline until a behavior-preserving adapter and golden test are added.
MLB publish/export package commands should enter through `models/mlb/cartridges/MLB-M0/lanes/` before touching delegated pipeline internals.
Do not promote MLB-RP36 into a standalone parent model; it should feed MLB-M0.
Before a new MLB slate, the prior day must have a results journal plus side prediction/backtest rows so lessons are based on warehouse-settled data.
Quiet-start, traffic-without-conversion, and quiet-first-five risks now suppress full-game side promotion unless another market expression is cleaner.
`MLB-M0_log.md` is the working log for warehouse/model changes that still need lane-specific proof.
knownLimitations: MLB-M0 run locks are file-based for now; they are not yet written into a shared model-run DB table.
Source inventory is intentionally broad until the MLB pregame chain is fully audited and split into smaller components.
